clue.text: Dancing fan not in time for jazzed up programmes

definitions.note: plural noun matching the plural sense of this media blend, treated as a mass noun

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so these four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's dance moves stop keeping time to the beat of jazzier television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges all of FAN NOT IN TIME, twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Television that mixes news or facts with entertainment is shows that have been jazzed up to keep viewers watching.

clue.text: Inexperienced girl's not faking it in going on top

indicators.note: in a down clue going on top means rising to the head of the column, so the named pair is shifted to the front

parts.note: someone not faking it is real or sincere: genuine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A risqué line about a young woman who is sincere about being on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a bedroom joke, but 'going on top' is a movement signal: in a down clue the pair named by 'in' rises to the head of the light.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is a theatrical stock role: a naive, innocent young woman.

clue.text: Thoroughly disheartened evangelist interrupting churchgoers for a bit of a nag

indicators.note: one piece interrupting another breaks into it, so it sits inside the congregation word

parts.note: a congregation is a flock, the faithful tended by a pastor

indicators.note: with the whole heart removed only the outside letters of the word evangelist remain

explanation.surface: A preacher with no spirit left disrupts the worshippers, nagging them a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thoroughly disheartened' removes the entire heart of the word, not just its single middle letter, leaving only its two ends; 'interrupting' breaks into the congregation word.
explanation.definitionFit: Part of a horse's leg, the tufted joint above the hoof, so a part of an old horse or nag.

clue.text: Steady current's drawn tide away

indicators.note: tide drawn away suggests the letters are pulled out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A constant flow of water has dragged the tide out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges DRAWN TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind is a steady prevailing wind blowing toward the equator, a regular current of air.

clue.text: Conclude there's no leaving hell

indicators.note: the word no leaving the longer word means those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: Dante's Inferno is hell, a fiery underworld
taken as written

explanation.surface: Deduce that once in hell there is no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Dealing with army officer, vocally

indicators.note: spoken out, so the officer's title is matched by its pronunciation rather than spelling

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking military officer, as in field marshal

explanation.surface: Handling troops, a commander gives orders out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means relating to war and the military, so concerned with soldiers and armies.

clue.text: Stuffing for tuna utilised for molluscs

indicators.note: the answer is the stuffing found inside the words tuna utilised

explanation.surface: A recipe using a filling for fish, perhaps of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing for' points to the run inside tuNA UTILIsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautiluses are cephalopods with chambered spiral shells, a kind of sea mollusc.

clue.text: Sort out getting involved in attacking way traders make money

indicators.note: one piece getting involved in another is placed within it

parts.note: bombarding with artillery is shelling

indicators.note: sorted out letters are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to fix a problem by going on the offensive, like a trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives ORTS from Sort, and 'getting involved in' sets that inside the bombardment word. Short selling profits from falling prices, which is why traders take the risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Short selling means selling borrowed stock hoping to buy it back cheaper, profiting when prices fall.

clue.text: Eat nuts after wasted meal

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the synonym for wasted

parts.note: slang for drunk or stoned: high

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of Eat go haywire

explanation.surface: A stoned person with the munchies is told to eat a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' scrambles Eat, and 'after' puts that result behind the slang word. High tea is a British early-evening cooked meal.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a British early-evening meal, often cooked, served with tea in place of dinner.

clue.text: Warning about fish shaking a lot

indicators.note: the warning word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of a flying ball

indicators.note: shaking off a letter means it is shed from the fish's name

parts.note: tuna is a large sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A caution that a fish is wriggling violently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like a quantity, but the noun lot here is one's fate; 'shaking' sheds the article from the fish and 'about' wraps the golfer's cry round it.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's fate or destiny, what chance hands out.

clue.text: Source of grievance in Greece and Spain: crippling German bills

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration letter for Spain (España)

indicators.note: a crippling blow twists things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Greece and Spain suffer under ruinous German demands during the euro debt crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crippling' scrambles the German demand; Greece and Spain suggest the euro crisis, but Spain only gives its car-plate letter and the definition is Greece's long-standing grievance against the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon sculptures taken to Britain by Lord Elgin, whose return Greece demands, a long-running grievance.

clue.text: Author dashed off a part

parts.note: to dash off is to run away, past tense ran
some means a portion, part of a whole

explanation.surface: A writer quickly scribbles a part for a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English writer, best known for the children's book Swallows and Amazons.

clue.text: Two swimmers, the first perceived in sound barrier

indicators.note: only the first fish is taken as heard, spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a ray is a flat sea fish
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A pair of swimmers hear something at the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first perceived in sound' asks only the first fish to be pronounced, so its spelling changes while the second keeps its written form; 'sound barrier' suggests aircraft but is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of rails, a barrier along a balcony or path.

clue.text: Mark requiring second kiss

parts.note: a peck is a light quick kiss

explanation.surface: A man called Mark needs a further smooch.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a small spot or mark, a tiny blemish.

clue.text: Current slump needs correcting: Number 10 is fronting push

indicators.note: the figure ten is fronting, placed before, the abbreviation for number

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a word that needs correcting has its letters set right in a new order

parts.note: the figure 10 written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Downing Street must fix an economic slump with a new current of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs correcting' rearranges slump as MPULS; ten as IO, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulsion is a driving force or impetus, a push that sets something in motion.

clue.text: Pity? It's lacking, whence Dracula's destructive urge

indicators.note: pity lacking it means those two letters are removed from it

parts.note: the word It, with the apostrophe-s read as is
Count Dracula comes from Transylvania, a region of Romania

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is a lack of compassion in the Transylvanian count's urge to destroy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IT from PITY to leave PY, then add ROMANIA, Dracula's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsive urge to start fires, a destructive impulse.

clue.text: With spin, one's taken in by Cameron? I see what you mean

indicators.note: the pieces are taken in, held inside, the party chief

parts.note: David Cameron was leader of the UK Conservative Party
the Roman numeral I is one
PR, public relations, is political spin

explanation.surface: A politician's media spin is swallowed by the then Tory leader, who claims he understands.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'see': a person reading lips understands speech by watching, so the phrase I see what you mean is literally true. 'taken in by' places the pair inside the party chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads lips literally sees what you are saying, a witty cryptic twist.

clue.text: U2 fans are so unrewarded

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as fans are
Bono is the lead singer of the Irish band U2, standing for the band

explanation.surface: Followers of the rock band go without payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work is done for the public good without a fee.

clue.text: Character eating is oppressed by burning fondness for the cream

indicators.note: the character is eating, swallowing, the other pieces

parts.note: an em is a printing character width, used as a unit

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is sits under, weighed down by, the synonym for burning

parts.note: lit means set alight, burning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a burning passion for the best people feels oppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oppressed by' works only in a down clue, where the later word sits beneath; 'eating' has the printing unit swallow both. The cream means the elite, the best of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is a preference for rule or recognition by an elite, the best few.

clue.text: It's hot filling tea cups etc

indicators.note: the word for hot fills the word for tea, going in its middle

parts.note: cha or char is slang for tea
in, as in fashionable: what's hot is in

explanation.surface: Boiling water poured into tea cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts the word for fashionable inside slang for tea; hot as fashionable is the step most solvers miss, since the surface suggests boiling water.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain crockery, such as cups and saucers.

clue.text: It's coming to a point where a Liberal is propping up right-winger in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below, propping up, those above them

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political scene where a Liberal holds up a Tory leader in coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is propping up' only works in a down clue, where the article and party letter sit beneath the Tory and the in-charge abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone tapers to its apex, so something cone-shaped narrows to a point.

clue.text: Troublemaker, one using trendy quotations?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as IN (trendy) plus CITER (one quoting), a person whose quotes are fashionable

explanation.surface: A stirrer is someone fond of fashionable quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inciter stirs others up to violence or unrest, the very model of a troublemaker.

clue.text: Emphatic confession of one telling stories about sun worship

indicators.note: the confession goes around the abbreviation for sun

parts.words: Emphatic confession of one telling stories
parts.note: a fibber's emphatic admission would be I do lie
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A liar admits fervent devotion to a sun god.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside I DO LIE after the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to worship or adore them excessively.

clue.text: Fellow in Macbeth, say, ending on high

indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter rises to the top

parts.note: Macbeth was Thane of Cawdor, a Scottish nobleman

explanation.surface: A man in Shakespeare's Scottish play finishes his part in elevated style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending on high' moves the last letter of THANE, E, to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethan is a man's first name, and crosswords treat a forename as any fellow or man.

clue.text: Conveyance from one endlessly gracious in The Faerie Queene

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the fairy queen's name

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant or gracious

explanation.surface: A carriage from a kind figure in Spenser's epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the last letter from the synonym for gracious, and 'in' places the result with the numeral inside the queen's name. Mab is the fairy queen of folklore, though Spenser's queen is Gloriana.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a small hired taxi, a conveyance for passengers.

clue.text: Like ugly little chap? Snog him excitably

indicators.note: excited letters jump around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goblin-like man gets a passionate kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitably' rearranges SNOG HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a squat, ugly little creature of folklore, so gnome-like describes such a fellow.

clue.text: Make out sporting contest in Ascot?

parts.note: to neck is slang for kissing passionately, making out
a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Couples kissing at a horse race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, but here it is the broad cravat, an example of a necktie, so the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide neck scarf, one example of formal neckwear.

clue.text: French correspondent is a Pulitzer Prize winner

parts.note: Norman French was the language of Normandy
a mailer is one who sends letters

explanation.surface: A journalist from France has won a top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer, US novelist, won the Pulitzer Prize twice, for The Armies of the Night and The Executioner's Song.
